stories.title: Host–microbe interactions in engineered immunocompetent human gut tissues
stories.takeaway: Researchers report engineered human gut tissue incorporating immune competence to investigate host–microbe interactions.
stories.what_happened: A Nature article published November 18 introduces an engineered human intestinal tissue approach for examining microbial interactions in an immune-containing context.
stories.why_it_matters: Integrating tissue and immune components may make human-relevant intestinal model systems more informative.
stories.caveat: Engineered tissues cannot fully reproduce systemic immunity or the full intestinal ecosystem.

stories.title: Closest relatives of poxviruses prevail in human and animal guts worldwide
stories.takeaway: Researchers identify a widespread group of large DNA viruses, termed egoviruses, in animal and human digestive systems.
stories.what_happened: A November 18 Nature paper describes diverse gut-associated egoviruses phylogenetically close to poxviruses, including a prevalent human-associated lineage.
stories.why_it_matters: Expands the known gut virome beyond commonly studied bacteriophages and raises new ecological questions.
stories.caveat: Genomic detection and evolutionary relatedness do not establish pathogenicity or effects on human health.

stories.title: Space-map: 3D single-cell atlas reconstruction from serial sections
stories.takeaway: Space-map reconstructs three-dimensional tissue architecture from large spatial transcriptomic and proteomic datasets.
stories.what_happened: A November 19 Nature Methods paper reports computational alignment of serial sections, including millions of profiled cells from intestinal tissue and a colon polyp.
stories.why_it_matters: Three-dimensional mapping could improve interpretation of epithelial crypt organization and tissue heterogeneity.
stories.caveat: Reconstruction accuracy depends on section quality and registration; spatial mapping alone does not establish functional mechanisms.

stories.title: Intestinal goblet cell defect is linked to immune dysregulation in multiple sclerosis
stories.takeaway: A new study investigates associations between intestinal goblet-cell abnormalities and immune dysregulation in multiple sclerosis.
stories.what_happened: A November 19 Scientific Reports article examines an intestinal epithelial feature in the context of a systemic immune-mediated disease.
stories.why_it_matters: Highlights how mucosal epithelial biology can inform research beyond gastrointestinal disorders.
stories.caveat: The reported link should not be interpreted as proof that goblet-cell changes cause multiple sclerosis.

stories.title: A glucose-powered artificial neuroimmune axis for metabolic control
stories.takeaway: Researchers describe a synthetic glucose-responsive neuroimmune strategy for regulating metabolism.
stories.what_happened: A November 18 Nature article reports an engineered neuroimmune axis designed to connect glucose sensing with metabolic control.
stories.why_it_matters: Illustrates the expanding scope of engineered biological feedback systems and translational bioengineering.
stories.caveat: Experimental metabolic control does not establish long-term safety or effectiveness in patients.
